findings: Ring rho is undetermined, not a pass: 0.67 (SE 0.38) reported, 0.75 (SE 0.36) in the replication; per-world values run from -2.1 to 1.0.
Ring D at budget is not determined: 0.343 reported, 0.137 in the replication (8 lab episodes; per world -0.07 to 0.28).

Ring sigma fails its bar in both runs (0.036 and 0.043), but its SE from 4 worlds is itself uncertain (0.009 reported, 0.020 replicated). On the ring the prior-mean policy beats P0 (replication: item-paired L difference 0.019, SE 0.003), so against the better no-experiment policy sigma is 0.030 (reported run) and 0.022 (replication). On gliders at full size P0 beats the prior mean in all families.
'The ring fails the sigma bar more than gliders' holds for the ridge family only (0.036-0.043 against 0.065); gliders with the net (0.030) and the amortised net (0.039) is level with the ring.

Gliders rho at full size: bootstrap P(rho <= 0.7) is 0.19 for the ridge at 2 episodes, 0.055 and 0.011 for the net at 2 and 8, and 0 in the other cells of the 2 and 8 episode columns; 'fails' is clear for the amortised net and for the ridge from 8 episodes.

Simulator cost: the 0.164 CPU-s per member-tick is a whole tiny process; the same file gives 0.104 marginal, and the checker's bench 0.191 CPU-s (0.138 wall-s). The rate is known to about +-30%, so 4 cores x 8 h buy 0.8 to 1.5 times round 4's full recipe (1.0 reported), at least 4.8 times the shrunk recipe and 7 times P0's set.

Wall clock per rollout: 11.3 h (dry run) and 27.3 h (exam profile), not 10.4 and 26.4; corrected above. The reference ladder for a single hidden world is 15.7 core-hours (C, S, P0, prior mean at 1,024 episodes); 'about 12' is the three-world average.

Sandbox, tested with evaluator/sandbox.run as uid 65534 in all namespaces: (a) the CPU limit is per process: four forked children used 3.24 CPU-s under a 1 s limit, exit 0; (b) a process that calls setsid() survives the wall-clock stop and wrote a file 3 s after it; (c) /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm are shared: a file written by one sandboxed process was read by the next, so state can pass between items and from the agent to its predictor outside the frozen, size-limited submission. TASK.md declares each of these limits; none of this changes a reported number.

Sandbox, by reading the code: only <run>/hidden and PHYSIM2_HIDE are covered; other rollouts' workspaces (C's model, trained at the true theta) stay mounted and are protected by directory permissions alone. In the probe the scratch root was mode 0700, so the hidden-file reads failed on permissions as well (the public copy, which is not hidden, gave the same PermissionError); the tmpfs layer itself works (as root inside: hidden listing empty). `rollout --cmd` binds agents/ (the reference policies) into the agent's sandbox, and C's theta is on a command line. In the container fallback (uid drop only) the predictor sees /run_dir outside hidden/ (not run).
'Gliders is the only world with an exam' was true at commit 593071565; round5/vortexexam has since built a fed-vortex exam pilot.

After the fact: the gliders S rerun (design 12 -> 24, cross-fitted, a second lab budget on the same instance) followed the failed first run; it is smoke size and the report says so. The grader gives every item seed 0, so item-bootstrap SEs are a little optimistic.
